chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, and from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, altogether from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Similar to it, except that Yunus said, 'The whip is taken from its halfway point, so he is whipped with it, and similarly for the lesser (amount) and the greater (amount).'

key_terms.السَّوْطُ: The whip or lash used for corporal punishment
key_terms.نِصْفِهِ: Its halfway point, referring to the middle of the whip

ai.seo_question: How is the whip applied when punishing slaves according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural nuance of administering hadd punishment to slaves, emphasizing that the whip is drawn from its midpoint to ensure uniformity in the strike regardless of the total count. This detail reflects the Shia juristic focus on precision (adl) in legal penalties, ensuring the punishment is neither excessive nor deficient in its physical application. It underscores the distinct legal status of slaves in classical fiqh, where their punishment is often quantified relative to free persons but executed with specific technical rigor.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, and from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, altogether from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> similar to it, except that Yunus said, ‘The whip would be grabbed from its halfway, so he would whip with it, and similar to that is for the lesser (amount of lashes) and the more’.
